title: Urosepsis in an Older Adult
scenario: An 82-year-old female nursing-home resident is brought to the emergency department with new-onset confusion, decreased oral intake, and foul-smelling cloudy urine over the past two days.

lines: 82-year-old female brought from nursing home for 2 days of new confusion and lethargy. Staff report reduced oral intake and cloudy, foul-smelling urine. Baseline is alert and oriented x3 per family; currently oriented to self only. Skin warm and flushed. Indwelling urinary catheter in place for 3 weeks. Mucous membranes dry.
Two large-bore IV lines placed. Blood cultures x2 drawn, urinalysis and urine culture obtained from catheter port. Lactate and CBC sent. Cardiac monitor and continuous pulse oximetry applied.
30 mL/kg isotonic crystalloid bolus initiated. Broad-spectrum IV antibiotic administered after cultures obtained. Existing catheter removed and replaced per order.
Client more responsive, now oriented to self and place. Skin cooler, less flushed. Urine output improving via new catheter. Reports feeling less foggy.

tabs.title: Laboratory Report
rows: Cloudy, leukocyte esterase +, nitrites +, WBC > 100/hpf, many bacteria

lines: Acetaminophen 650 mg PO every 6 hours PRN
Isotonic crystalloid 30 mL/kg IV bolus now
Obtain blood cultures x2 and urine culture before antibiotics
Broad-spectrum IV antibiotic now, then per protocol
Remove and replace indwelling urinary catheter
Measure serum lactate now and repeat in 4 hours
Strict intake and output; notify provider for urine output < 30 mL/hr

children.subject: Medical-Surgical
children.rationale: Acute confusion, fever, hypotension, and tachycardia together signal a systemic infectious response and possible sepsis, requiring prompt intervention. The home medication and chronic history are background, not urgent cues.

children.subject: Medical-Surgical
children.stem: For each finding, click to specify whether it supports a urinary source of infection, a systemic septic response, or both. Each finding may support more than one.

rows.text: Nitrites and leukocyte esterase positive on urinalysis

children.rationale: Positive nitrites/esterase, cloudy urine, and a chronic catheter localize infection to the urinary tract, while elevated lactate and hypotension reflect the systemic septic response. Leukocytosis supports both the infection and the systemic reaction to it.

children.subject: Medical-Surgical
children.stem: Complete the sentence. The nurse determines that the priority problem is {1}, and the most immediate goal is to {2}.

choices.text: restore circulating volume and blood pressure

children.rationale: The hypotension and elevated lactate show inadequate tissue perfusion from sepsis, the greatest immediate threat. Rapid fluid resuscitation to restore volume and blood pressure takes priority over comfort or reorientation measures.

children.subject: Medical-Surgical
children.stem: For each intervention, click to specify whether it is indicated or contraindicated for this client at this time.

rows.text: Obtain blood and urine cultures before starting antibiotics
Administer a 30 mL/kg isotonic crystalloid bolus
Delay antibiotics until final culture results return
Remove and replace the chronic indwelling catheter
Withhold IV fluids to prevent overload

children.rationale: Early cultures, prompt fluid resuscitation, and source control by replacing the infected catheter are core sepsis interventions. Delaying antibiotics for final cultures or withholding fluids would worsen perfusion and outcomes.

children.subject: Medical-Surgical
children.stem: Which actions should the nurse take to implement the sepsis orders? Select all that apply.

options.text: Administer the broad-spectrum IV antibiotic after cultures are drawn
Infuse the ordered isotonic fluid bolus
Repeat the serum lactate as ordered
Hold the antibiotic until the fever resolves
Restrict all IV fluids to keep the client dry

children.rationale: Timely antibiotics after cultures, fluid resuscitation, strict output monitoring, and a repeat lactate are the actions that carry out the sepsis bundle. Holding antibiotics or restricting fluids would delay treatment and worsen perfusion.

children.subject: Medical-Surgical
children.stem: Which findings indicate the treatment has been effective? Select all that apply.

options.text: Client now oriented to self and place

children.rationale: Rising blood pressure, slowing heart rate, improving mentation, and a falling temperature all show the septic response is resolving. Persistent hypotension or oliguria would indicate ongoing shock, not improvement.
